evidence.note: Created three explicit ordered milestone tasks via TaskCreate that mirror the phase gate: build full API in model.py, copy to model_optimized.py and confirm benchmark PASS, then run <=8 optimization experiments keeping fastest — each with an embedded done-condition.

Respected the correctness-then-optimization ordering: wrote model.py, ran JAX-vs-PyTorch parity check (step 49), fixed TF32, marked build+parity tasks complete, and only then copied the frozen checkpoint to model_optimized.py and confirmed the shim before optimizing.

Optimization treated as a bounded sequence of 8 discretely-named, individually-scoped experiments (compile, reduce-overhead, max-autotune, batched vision, coordinate-descent, SDPA, vision SDPA, enable_gqa), several gated by offline parity verification (144-150, 167) before applying.

Independently checkable closing milestones: smoke test + checkpoint/shim integrity verification, and model.py checkpoint correctness re-verified on CUDA before final task completion — the frozen checkpoint was protected end-to-end.

reasoning: The agent built an explicit, ordered milestone hierarchy (build API -> establish parity -> freeze checkpoint -> bounded optimization), each with a checkable done-signal, respected the correctness checkpoint, pointed the shim at the optimized file, and ran optimization as eight distinct scoped experiments with parity gates — matching anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because the eight experiments were discovered iteratively rather than pre-planned as a coherent hypothesis-driven search, and the API was built as a single write with no explicit risk-ordering of hardest-to-parity components first.
